title: Quick check: Handling Keyboard Events

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Handling Keyboard Events”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Key presses should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Key presses should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Keyboard Events: Key presses should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Key presses?
options: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Keyboard Events: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Handling Keyboard Events” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Keyboard Events: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
